title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 11 — Gravitation

explanation: Every pair of masses in the universe attracts each other with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers. This inverse-square relationship means the force drops off very quickly with distance — doubling the separation reduces the force to one quarter.

variables.meaning: Gravitational force between the two masses
Distance between the centers of the two masses

workedExample.scenario: Two 10 kg masses are 2 m apart.
workedExample.result: F ≈ 1.67 × 10⁻⁹ N (extremely small — gravity between everyday objects is negligible)

commonMistakes: Forgetting that r is measured between the CENTERS of the masses, not their surfaces.
Not squaring r — a very common arithmetic slip given the inverse-SQUARE relationship.
genZNote: This formula is why gravity between two people standing near each other is basically zero, but gravity between you and an entire planet is very much not.
